arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Phillips argued that the jury instructions did not apply the correct legal standard for retaliation.
Mr. Donati argued that reassigning and suspending White without pay constituted discrimination.
Justice Breyer asked if excluding a woman from a key meeting could harm her career and count as a violation.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case centers on whether federal law protects employees from non-economic workplace mistreatment after filing discrimination charges. The dispute involves the scope of retaliation claims under Title VII.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Burlington Northern wants the Court to limit retaliation claims to tangible economic losses.
White wants the Court to recognize non-economic workplace mistreatment as actionable retaliation.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Burlington Northern argues that minor reassignments and suspensions do not meet the legal threshold for retaliation.
White argues that excluding an employee from work activities after a charge constitutes illegal retaliation.

paragraphs: The outcome defines the scope of federal protections for employees who report discrimination. It determines whether employers can impose non-economic penalties without legal consequence. This standard affects workplace conduct and employee rights nationwide.
